comments.body:
## Owner decisions and M1 preparation retained while branch admission is blocked

PR #5 has been merged into `develop` at `0012a172492515e282be09c37921f4014a451e64`. The next increment remains this feature issue; it has not been rerouted through a chore/documentation issue to bypass its prerequisite.

Two owner decisions are now confirmed:

1. **Administrator recovery:** in `setup_administrator` / `selected_ha_user` modes, require a currently proven HA administrator **and explicit installation-console confirmation**. The two authorities must be bound to the same identity/installation. No first-browser fallback or silent switch to `all_ha_administrators`.
2. **Home Assistant outage:** an already valid session may query locally retained data until its original absolute expiry. **Mutations and administrative actions remain blocked.** Recheck current local membership/policy for every read; known suspension/unlinking applies immediately. Do not renew/create a session while HA is unavailable, and distinguish explicit credential rejection from availability failure.

The planned recovery contract uses an expiring identity/installation/channel/mapping-bound request, console approval outside the browser surface, fresh HA proof on completion, and one atomic grant/consumption/receipt/audit/outbox transaction. Tests must cover both missing authorities, target substitution, expiry, stale mapping, suspended target, replay, concurrent completion and rollback. This is prospective design, not an implemented recovery CLI/API.

Preparation outside the checkout updates the **existing** `household-identity` and `platform-foundation` owners in the installed twenty-section SDD format. It adds 22 identity cases (52 total) and 14 platform cases (34 total), with reciprocal requirement/case tables and updated numeric budgets. The new cases cover authentication/protocol rejection, bounded offline-read leases and local revocation, dual-authority recovery, real-file migration/rollback/races, scoped replay, restart, backup and channel/instance refusal. These are **planned cases; zero new application tests have executed**.

Both prospective SDDs pass unchanged pinned `validateSddMarkdown`, `validateSddDraftConsistency` and exact canonical-heading checks against the merged PR #5 file inventory. The seven upstream source copies were verified against their Git blob IDs first. A five-file prospective documentation/catalog patch passes `git apply --check` against that exact base. Capability statuses/evidence arrays remain unchanged; no absent application evidence is disguised as tooling.

Implementation after managed branch readiness will introduce the real backend with pure domain policies and semantic application ports, separate HA/SQLite/HTTP adapters, a distinct 100% supported backend coverage gate, and import checks against actual product modules. Existing tooling/Node/documentation checks and the strict CI aggregate remain required. No runtime source or application test has been authored before the branch gate.

The actual prerequisite failure is now linked to the existing upstream report: https://github.com/vypdev/copilot/issues/777#issuecomment-6486050904. The unchanged reader reproduces `owner-paths-invalid`; the unchanged catalog validator returns exactly thirty absent-evidence errors on ten unimplemented proposed capabilities. [The failed Action](https://github.com/vypdev/domus/actions/runs/40804494274) published no branch or expected ref suitable for exceptional recovery. Do not retry unchanged input, create a substitute branch, fabricate evidence or modify Copilot to bypass this.

All twenty-nine protected installed-resource hashes still match, and the repository checkout remains clean at the merged base. The read-only Chrome HA version check did not extract credentials or modify household configuration/entities. Live identity, Ingress and actual deployment acceptance remain unproven.

comments.author: efraespada
comments.body:
The catalog/bootstrap blocker is resolved. These maintainer answers use the owner's confirmed architecture and the supported HA protocols. The immutable feature base `0012a172492515e282be09c37921f4014a451e64` does contain `specs/` and both registered owners. Preserve those contracts. A focused implementation companion under `platform-foundation` is acceptable; it must reference `household-identity` rather than create another owner of member/authorization state. Do not infer missing repository evidence from the workflow's unrelated default-branch checkout.

SDD Q1: Supervisor uses the fixed internal Core proxy `http://supervisor/core/api/` and WebSocket `ws://supervisor/core/websocket`, with `homeassistant_api: true` and the runtime-provided SUPERVISOR_TOKEN kept out of logs/database/browser. This credential authenticates adapter transport only, never the human caller. Standalone requires an operator-controlled DOMUS_HA_URL in installation configuration, validated as an explicit HTTP(S) origin without userinfo, query or fragment; LAN HTTP is supported for the owner's local HA, HTTPS verifies certificates. Build the known Core paths from that origin, reject request/body/forwarded-header endpoint overrides, disable automatic redirects and environment-proxy inheritance, and apply bounded timeouts/message sizes. Missing/invalid configuration fails startup readiness without exposing protected APIs. An unavailable configured HA permits only the owner's existing-session bounded local-read policy; writes/setup/recovery fail closed. Endpoint changes require deliberate operator reconfiguration/restart, invalidate sessions and unfinished authorization/recovery flows, and preserve household/business history; connecting a different HA instance must not silently relink identities or widen grants.

SDD Q2: Use deployment-specific supported HA identity adapters behind the same semantic PrincipalVerifier port. Standalone is an HA public OAuth client: no central registration or client secret; client_id is the exact operator-configured Domus public origin URL, with a fixed callback on that same host/port (`/api/v1/auth/callback`). Require state plus S256 PKCE, exact callback/client binding, bounded single-use pending attempts, HttpOnly/SameSite session cookies, Origin/CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated mutations, server-side token exchange/current-user proof and no token persistence. Never construct origins from Host, forwarded or Ingress headers. Supervisor's normal Ingress profile uses HA's existing native login, with no second OAuth login or public callback: accept identity metadata only on the dedicated Ingress listener from the actual Supervisor peer 172.30.32.2, with proxy-header address rewriting disabled and no direct published port. Missing X-Remote-User-Id fails authentication; use its ID only as the candidate subject, then authoritatively recheck that subject's current active human account and HA administrator source through Core over the fixed private adapter. The installation token's own administrator privilege must never be assigned to that subject. Treat names as display text, not proof. Standalone never accepts these headers. X-Ingress-Path may supply a validated UI base path only after that transport boundary is verified; it never supplies an OAuth origin or administrator grant. Core protocol/schema and actual Ingress/browser acceptance need tests; a fabricated header fixture cannot count as live proof. This is the equivalent supported HA authentication path already allowed by the owning architecture, not a replacement password store, gateway or second MCP.

SDD Q3: Provide a local `domus-admin recovery approve <request-id>` console entrypoint, available to the installation operator inside the owned container/host console (for standalone, docker exec; for Supervisor, the installation's controlled App/container console). It is not an HTTP approval endpoint or an HA option that silently approves. Read the pending request from the installation's SQLite database, display its exact target HA user ID plus safely rendered verified name, instance ID, Stable/Edge channel, mapping/revision, creation and expiry, and require an explicit confirmation of that exact target ID. Requests expire after 10 minutes, are identity/installation/channel/mapping-bound and single-use. Completion still requires fresh proof of the same current HA administrator; console possession alone grants nothing. Atomically record the explicit recovered administrator grant, consume approval and commit receipt/audit/outbox while preserving the configured mapping/history. Wrong target, missing authority, expiry, suspended target, stale mapping, replay and concurrent completion must not duplicate or widen grants. An identical currently authorized retry resolves its original receipt; revoked access cannot read that receipt. The command is a proposed entrypoint to implement and test, not an existing binary or a claim of live acceptance.

Primary protocol references:
- https://contributors.home-assistant.io/apps/guides/communication/
- https://contributors.home-assistant.io/apps/guides/ingress/
- https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/internals/auth-api/
- https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2026.10.4/homeassistant/components/config/auth.py

Keep all repository prose, code, comments, tests and generated issue/PR content English. Maintain the separate 100% supported backend coverage gate and real application import graph from the first source file. Do not weaken current authorization, idempotency, channel isolation, supported first-release scope or the no-Copilot-change rule.

comments.author: efraespada
comments.body:
SDD Q1: The issue author explicitly confirmed these configurable defaults today. For this M1 surface use the following permission-by-action matrix (A=administrator, D=adult, R=restricted, V=viewer; all require current active membership unless the bootstrap/recovery rule explicitly applies): household/member public-summary read=A,D,R,V; read/update own locale/notification preferences=A,D,R,V, scoped to the caller; read another member's private preferences=denied by default; request own pending enrollment=any currently verified unlinked HA human, with no active access or role grant; activate/link/suspend/archive members or assign explicit roles=A; change household profiles/member exceptions, administrator mapping or protected settings=A; read an operation receipt=its authenticated actor with the operation's current permission and household scope, never key possession alone. Initial household setup requires an explicit action by a currently proven HA administrator. Recovery is a separate dual-authority flow requiring the same currently proven HA administrator and local-console confirmation, not an ordinary configurable permission. For subsequent domain increments retain the confirmed defaults: adults operate ordinary household work/supplies and may approve restricted performers' completions; restricted members may complete assigned tasks and add their own shopping requests; viewers query authorized data only; all edit their own preferences. Administrator-only actions include point/verification/automation configuration and privileged corrections. These statements do not claim those later domain APIs are implemented by this increment. Precedence for supported configurable actions is hard identity/scope/domain constraints, then explicit member exception, then household profile adjustment, then predefined role default, then deny if undefined. Member exceptions may allow or deny a supported ordinary action, so they can expand a household profile denial as already owner-approved; they cannot grant administrator identity, bypass suspension/unlinking, cross scope, bypass restricted-performer adult verification or violate a domain invariant. Conflicting allow/deny entries at the same level are rejected while preserving prior policy. Only a currently authorized administrator changes profiles/exceptions; ordinary members never edit their own authority. Current policy is checked inside command transactions and before receipt lookup, with expected revisions and cache invalidation. Source-derived administration in all_ha_administrators cannot be silently demoted by an ordinary profile edit: change its authorized mapping or live HA source, preserving independent explicit grants and last-administrator safety. HA outage never extends cached authority or permits mutation.

This is the new answer for clarification round 2, not a replacement of round 1. Retain all previously confirmed endpoint, per-target authentication and console-recovery answers. The owner keeps all product domains/both targets in the first release; this increment establishes their shared identity/persistence foundation.

comments.author: efraespada
comments.body:
These answers restate the confirmed decisions for the new issue fingerprint after selecting the complete companion. Use action `companion`, capability `platform-foundation`, NEW path `specs/platform-foundation-identity-sqlite.md`; preserve the original platform/identity owners and use distinct new case IDs. The companion is explicitly approved instead of an 18,000-character update appendix. Keep all behavior and risk coverage; do not shorten the product scope to fit an appendix.

SDD Q1: Standalone uses HA authorization code with state and S256 PKCE: fixed operator-configured HA origin and exact Domus public client/callback origin, server-side form token exchange, bounded single-use attempts and server-owned sessions, no central client registration/client secret. Current-user WebSocket proof must authenticate the exchanged user's token and obtain its exact ID plus Boolean administrator flag; reject malformed/correlated-to-another-request, inactive/rejected/expired proof and technical credentials presented to the human API. Supervisor instead uses native HA Ingress login on a private listener accepting only actual peer 172.30.32.2, proxy-header rewriting disabled, and requires remote user ID plus a fresh Core lookup of that active non-system human and its actual administrator source. Fixed supervisor Core proxy/token is transport authority only, never the human role. Missing identity fails closed; standalone never accepts Ingress identity headers. Core 2026.10.4 is the observed reference baseline; declare only independently tested Core/Supervisor protocol versions supported, retain a versioned contract matrix, and test the owner's current version before claiming live acceptance. Do not promise untested versions. Fixed upstream/configured origin, strict URL validation, no request-chosen hosts/redirects/proxies, bounded I/O and redacted errors apply. Existing valid sessions may query local data during HA outage only until original absolute expiry, rechecking current local policy/known revocation; no session extension or mutation while unavailable, and explicit HA rejection invalidates access rather than becoming an offline lease.

SDD Q2: Modes are all_ha_administrators (default, live inherited grant for each proven current HA admin), setup_administrator (designated proven setup HA admin), selected_ha_user (explicit active human selected by proven HA admin; selected human need not be an HA admin). Initial setup is explicit; first browser arrival never creates authority. Keep source provenance and independent explicit grants; mapping/source changes revoke inherited grants, never override suspension or technical-principal boundaries, and Domus edits cannot remove its last active effective administrator. The owner confirmed configurable defaults: administrator manages members, policy/settings and privileged corrections; adult handles ordinary daily work/supplies and may approve restricted performers; restricted completes assigned work and creates own shopping requests; viewer queries authorized data only; everyone edits own preferences. M1 matrix: public household/member-summary read=A,D,R,V; own preference read/update=A,D,R,V; pending self-enrollment=verified unlinked human without active access; member activation/linking/status/explicit role and profile/override/mapping edits=A; receipt lookup=original principal plus current operation permission/scope. Private preferences of another member are denied by default. Hard identity/scope/domain constraints outrank explicit member override, then household profile adjustment, then predefined defaults, then deny undefined actions. Supported ordinary exceptions may allow or deny and expand a profile denial; they cannot create administrator identity, bypass restricted-performer approval, cross scope or weaken invariants. Reject same-level contradictions, preserve prior policy, require administrator edits, optimistic revisions and transaction-time current-policy checks/cache invalidation. Configuration of point values, verification, automation and privileged corrections remains administrator-only.

SDD Q3: Current HA administrator requests recovery; local installation operator approves with proposed `domus-admin recovery approve <request-id>` inside the owned host/container console (docker exec for standalone; controlled App/container console for Supervisor). No HTTP approval route, shared PIN or implicit HA-options approval. Display request ID, exact verified target HA ID plus safely rendered display name, installation UUID, channel, mapping/revision, creation and expiry; require explicit confirmation of that exact target. Lifetime is ten minutes; bind approval to the same identity/installation/channel/mapping. Completion requires fresh proof that the same target is a current HA administrator and not suspended, then atomically commits an explicit recovery grant, consumed approval, receipt, audit and outbox while preserving mapping/history. Wrong identity/channel, missing authority, expiry, stale mapping or concurrency cannot widen/duplicate grants. Authorized identical replay returns the retained receipt; a later revoked actor cannot read it. Rollback leaves both request and grants unchanged. Console possession without fresh HA proof grants nothing.

SDD Q4: Database metadata contains a Domus application marker, schema version, persistent installation UUID and channel enum stable/edge. Match the configured installation/channel before any mutation; never silently regenerate identity for an existing database, adopt an unrelated database or open Stable data as Edge. Inspect future/unrelated schemas before journal/schema writes; migrations are explicit atomic SQL transactions and failures preserve recoverable prior state. Domain changes, scoped command receipt, audit and outbox commit together. Backup uses a consistent SQLite snapshot including identity/schema, business state, receipts/replay guards, audit and outbox; integrity/schema/identity verification precedes restore activation. A corrupt/future/wrong-instance-or-channel candidate cannot replace the active database. Preserve command key scope, canonical payload digest and durable result across restart, retention and restore so old retries cannot create effects. Activity cleanup must not delete replay protection. Production-to-Edge copying needs an explicit import/sanitization path, not automatic identity adoption. Credentials and HA tokens never enter these business tables or evidence.

SDD Q5: Use separate per-unit-of-work SQLite connections and BEGIN IMMEDIATE to serialize writers, with an initial 250 ms busy budget. Return bounded storage_busy/503 with retryable=true and Retry-After guidance when no writer slot is obtained; no partial effects. Check current local permissions inside the transaction before receipt lookup or new effects. Identical scoped key/payload returns its original result before treating its old expected revision as a new-write conflict; changed payload for the same key returns idempotency_conflict/409. New writes compare expected aggregate/policy revision and return revision_conflict/409 instead of overwriting. Do not automatically retry mutations with a new key, silently rebase stale edits or replay side effects. A client may deliberately retry the same request/key after temporary unavailability or a lost response, still subject to current authorization; stale-revision resolution requires explicit review/resubmission. Use deterministic clocks/failure injection and real-file connection/process/concurrency fixtures, without sleeps as business tests.

SDD Q6: Initial routes: GET /api/v1/session, GET /api/v1/household, POST /api/v1/household/setup, GET /api/v1/members, POST /api/v1/members/enroll, PATCH /api/v1/members/{member_id}, PATCH /api/v1/members/me/preferences, GET/PUT /api/v1/authorization, GET /api/v1/operations/{operation_id}, POST /api/v1/recovery/requests, POST /api/v1/recovery/{request_id}/complete; standalone GET /api/v1/auth/start and /api/v1/auth/callback plus POST /api/v1/auth/logout. No HTTP recovery approval. Strict typed request schemas forbid unknown fields, validate bounded IDs/text/timezone/enums, and require expected revisions plus Idempotency-Key for mutations; authenticated actor never comes from a submitted member ID. Return stable business IDs, state/revisions and operation ID; authorized replay returns original durable result. Safe envelope is {error:{code,message,correlation_id,retryable,details}}, with only allowlisted nonsecret details. Use 401 invalid/missing identity, 403 denied action, 404 absent/invisible scoped record, 409 revision/idempotency/last-admin conflict, 422 invalid input and 503 unavailable/busy; invalid/denied requests leave no business/receipt/audit/outbox effect. Cookie mutations require Origin/CSRF checks. Document exact DTOs/OpenAPI and response examples in the implementation; API schemas remain entrypoint DTOs, not domain models. No unrelated household-domain endpoints, product UI or publication are claimed by these routes.

SDD Q7: All authored backend modules, including unimported runtime files, have an independent coverage scope enforced at 100% executable statements/lines and branches as exposed by coverage.py/pytest-cov. No broad exclusions or test-only production branches; any genuine generated/third-party/non-executable declaration distinction must be explicit and cannot hide logic. Function metrics are enforced when supported, not invented where unavailable. Keep tooling, frontend and future HA integration scopes independent. Wire the actual domus package graph into the existing application import-linter contract: composition wires entrypoints/infrastructure; those adapters are independent; application depends only inward on domain/semantic ports; neither inner layer imports FastAPI, HA, HTTP/SQL clients or concrete I/O. Reject outward edges and cycles in actual modules as well as policy fixtures. Extend CI Check with the backend suite/coverage artifacts, frozen installs and strict aggregate needs; every PR update, including drafts/docs-only changes, must run every applicable suite. Existing installed Copilot resource hashes remain unchanged. Merge requires complete coverage and a current-head complete Bugbot review with no unresolved findings; skipped/neutral/incomplete review is not acceptance.

SDD Q8: This increment must prove the common use-case/API contracts under explicit Supervisor and standalone wiring with real SQLite and controlled protocol fixtures: fixed endpoint/config failures, identity spoofing/missing metadata, current HA source revocation, session/CSRF/origin behavior, per-mode role defaults, offline-read lease, recovery, restart/rollback/races and channel isolation. Supervisor fixtures must test the actual socket peer boundary and prefixed routing, not trust arbitrary forwarding headers. Standalone fixtures must prove OAuth state/PKCE/callback/current-user proof and rejection of Ingress/transport credentials as identity. Actual package installation, full UI/HA surface and Stable/Edge release acceptance remain tracked separately and are still mandatory for the first usable product. Use authorized Chrome on the owner's HA only with an identifiable experimental artifact, owned test data and cleanup; record exact versions/artifact/scenarios and honestly mark every unexecuted target/live case pending. Protocol fixtures or coverage alone cannot claim real HA/Ingress deployment acceptance. Keep the existing gateway and MCP unchanged.

comments.author: efraespada
comments.body: SDD Q2: Limit this M1 increment to the consistent backup/restore primitive and its real-file tests, not a new automatic backup scheduler/rotation product. The owner asked what these backups referred to; no daily/weekly frequency or retention option was approved. This implementation boundary is a technical sequencing decision, not a new owner-confirmed backup policy. In Supervisor, deployment packaging should include Domus state in the operator's normal HA backup mechanism using a consistent snapshot/appropriate hooks; HA owns its configured schedule and retention. For standalone in this increment, provide explicit local snapshot creation through the installation console and retain successful snapshots until the operator deliberately removes them; no automatic pruning. A pre-upgrade recovery snapshot and its compatible application/configuration pairing must be retained before destructive migration. Exact packaged schedule/retention and target-specific recovery-time acceptance are explicitly deferred to the deployment/operations gate, not dropped from first-release review. Concrete required restore target now: a new owned data directory for the SAME installation UUID and SAME stable/edge channel, with writes stopped, verified schema/application marker, integrity, manifest/checksum and identity before activation. A corrupt, future, wrong-instance or wrong-channel candidate cannot replace active data. Restore must reproduce all committed business records together with audit/outbox and command receipts/replay guards; authorized retry of an old key after restore cannot create another effect. The recovery point is the selected successful snapshot's committed checkpoint, visibly timestamped; there is no unproven 24-hour RPO or restoration-time SLA. Use a paired compatible image/schema for rollback. HA credentials and browser session tokens are excluded from business-state snapshots, so restored users reauthenticate normally. Packaging/live HA backup participation and operational retention/time objectives remain documented pending acceptance items; a SQLite fixture cannot claim them passed.
